PARULKULSHRESTHA

AN SUV allegedly ploughed
through a busy street in Jaipur on
Monday night, killing three peo-
ple and iniuring at least six others,
According to police, around
10 pm, Usmaan Khan (62), a fac-
tory owner and a Congress
leader, was driving his vehiclein
the Walled City area, the lanes of
which are typically congested.
Police are probing if he was un-
der the influence of alcohol.
Following the incident, the
Jaipur district Congress commit-
tee submitted a memorandumto
Jaipur Collector Jitendra Soni,
whichstated: “It was learnt from
the newspapers that Usman
Khan, the vice-president of Jaipur
City District Congress Committee,
ran over several people while
driving recklessly, in which three
people died and many were in-
jured. Therefore, Jaipur City
District Congress Committee de-
mands from the state govern-
ment that proper compensation
be given to the dead and injured
and the culprit be given the
harshest punishment.”
The incident took place un-
derthe jurisdiction of Nahargarh
police station. SHO Rameshwari
said, “The driver was caught
while trying to escape... We de-
tained him and conducted a
medical examination. An inves-
tigation is underway and we will
take action accordingly.”
Police said the accused hit
several vehicles, including two-
wheelers, over a500-metre dis-
tance. He first hit a scooter near
Santoshi Mata temple.
Around 10.30 am on
Tuesday, BJP MLA from Hawa
Mahal, Balmukund Acharya, led
a protest in front of the police
station, demanding compensa-
tion for families of those dead.

articles.text:
THE UNITED States said on Tuesday that 104% duties on imports from China will take effect shortly after midnight, even as the Trump administration moved to quickly start talks with other trading partners targeted by President Donald Trump's sweeping tariff plan. US stocks retreated on the news. Global markets had previously posted gains on hopes that Trump might be willing to negotiate down the array of country and product-specific trade barriers he is erecting around the world's largest consumer market.

The administration has scheduled talks with South Korea and Japan, two close allies and major trading partners, and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is due to visit next week. But the White House made clear that country-specific tariffs of upto 50% would nevertheless take effect at 12:01 am Eastern Time (0401 GMT), as planned. Those tariffs will be espedally steep for China, as Trump has ratcheted up duties on its imports to 104% in response to counter-tariffs Beijing announced last week. China has refused to bow to what it called "blackmail" and has vowed to "fight to the end". Administration officials said they would not prioritise negotiations with the world's No. 2
